candidate.title: ChIRP
candidate.scope: The middle ChIRP (Chromatin Isolation by RNA Purification) row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: ncRNA-associated chromatin is crosslinked and fragmented, selected with biotinylated tiling probes, captured on streptavidin magnetic beads, released by RNase treatment, and recovered as DNA. The matched Chu et al. 2011 implementation clarifies the release chemistry. ChIRP-seq denotes downstream sequencing of the recovered DNA, not a separate depicted alternative. FRT-Seq, CHART, the clipped PAL-seq text above, and chemical structures at the right are neighboring poster content, outside this card. The left contextual chromatin cartoon is not another workflow branch; no alternative target workflow is shown. The paper's separate RNA/protein outputs and split-probe experiments are not depicted branches here.

states.label: ncRNA-associated chromatin
features: A selected ncRNA (purple) is associated with a blue RNA-binding protein on nucleosomal chromatin (black DNA and gray nucleosomes).
This is the input association to be retained; the leftmost repeated cartoon illustrates the assay concept rather than a separate material branch.

states.label: Extracted DNA from ncRNA-associated chromatin
features: Terminal blue line is labeled DNA; no strand count, end chemistry, adapters or barcode are specified.
The sequencing substrate is co-purified genomic DNA, representing chromatin association with the selected RNA; it is not cDNA copied from the target RNA.
The drawing ends at extracted DNA. The primary paper establishes its downstream use as the input to sequencing-library construction.

Genomic mapping identifies regions associated with the selected RNA in fixed chromatin. Direct versus protein-mediated contact, exact contact bases and functional consequences are not established by this readout alone.
Off-target probe hybridization can contribute background DNA; enrichment and RNase-dependent release do not guarantee perfect specificity.

operations.label:
Crosslink
Fragment
operations.description: Fix the associations among ncRNA, protein and chromatin, then fragment the chromatin into material accessible for capture. The primary text identifies sonication as the fragmentation step.
operations.mechanism: Crosslinking preserves the associated complexes; sonication fragments and solubilizes chromatin. The generic diagram does not choose among crosslinking chemistries.
operations.information_effect: Preserves the RNA-chromatin association on recoverable DNA fragments rather than recording a direct molecular contact coordinate.

operations.description: Attach the biotinylated probe-RNA complexes and their associated chromatin to streptavidin magnetic beads, enriching target-containing complexes from the surrounding fragmented chromatin.

operations.label: RNase H
operations.description: Release associated DNA/protein material from the bead-bound RNA/probe complex by RNase treatment. The diagram labels this step RNase H; the matched primary implementation uses RNase A together with RNase H, as recorded in c_rnase_release.
operations.mechanism: For the paper-supported implementation, RNase A plus RNase H digestion disrupts the RNA bridge and preferentially elutes associated DNA rather than DNA retained solely by direct probe-DNA hybridization.
operations.information_effect: Converts bead-bound capture into an RNA-dependent DNA eluate; preferential release is a selection principle, not proof of perfect biological specificity.
